title: एकोनविंशत्यधिकत्रिशततमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: The son of Vyasa climbs a mountain, sits in a lonely place and fixes his mind, and then rises from Kailasa into the sky. He passes the Malaya mountain where the apsarases Urvashi and Purvachitti dwell, who marvel at the young brahmin sage.
summary.kn: ವ್ಯಾಸಪುತ್ರ ಪರ್ವತ ಏರಿ ನಿರ್ಜನ ಸ್ಥಳದಲ್ಲಿ ಕುಳಿತು ಮನಸ್ಸು ಸ್ಥಿರಗೊಳಿಸಿ ಕೈಲಾಸದಿಂದ ಆಕಾಶಕ್ಕೆ ಹಾರುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಊರ್ವಶಿ-ಪೂರ್ವಚಿತ್ತಿ ವಾಸಿಸುವ ಮಲಯ ಪರ್ವತ ದಾಟಿ ಹೋಗುವಾಗ ಅಪ್ಸರೆಯರು ಬಾಲ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮರ್ಷಿಯನ್ನು ಕಂಡು ಬೆರಗಾಗುತ್ತಾರೆ.
summary.hi: व्यासपुत्र पर्वत पर चढ़कर निर्जन स्थान में बैठते और मन स्थिर करते हैं, फिर कैलास से आकाश में उठते हैं। वे मलय पर्वत के पास से गुजरते हैं जहाँ उर्वशी और पूर्वचित्ति रहती हैं और जो युवा ब्रह्मर्षि को देख विस्मित होती हैं।
summary.te: వ్యాస పుత్రుడు పర్వతం ఎక్కి నిర్జన ప్రదేశంలో కూర్చుని మనసు నిలిపి కైలాసం నుండి ఆకాశంలోకి ఎగురుతాడు. ఊర్వశి, పూర్వచిత్తి ఉండే మలయ పర్వతాన్ని దాటగా అప్సరసలు యువ బ్రహ్మర్షిని చూసి ఆశ్చర్యపడతారు.
summary.ta: வியாசரின் மகன் மலை ஏறித் தனிமையான இடத்தில் அமர்ந்து மனத்தை நிலைநிறுத்தி கைலாசத்திலிருந்து வானில் எழுகிறார். ஊர்வசியும் பூர்வசித்தியும் வாழும் மலய மலையைக் கடக்கும்போது அப்சரஸ்கள் இளம் பிரம்மரிஷியைக் கண்டு வியக்கின்றனர்.
summary.ml: വ്യാസപുത്രൻ പർവ്വതം കയറി, ഏകാന്ത സ്ഥലത്ത് ഇരുന്ന് മനസ്സ് ഉറപ്പിക്കുന്നു, പിന്നീട് കൈലാസത്തിൽനിന്ന് ആകാശത്തേക്ക് ഉയരുന്നു. ഊർവശിയും പൂർവ്വചിത്തിയും വസിക്കുന്ന മലയ പർവ്വതം കടക്കുമ്പോൾ, ആ യുവ ബ്രാഹ്മണമുനിയെക്കണ്ട് അപ്സരസ്സുകൾ അദ്ഭുതപ്പെടുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 12.319; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Jun 16 2021

verses.text: भीष्म उवाच

meaning.en: Bhishma said:

verses.text:
गिरिपृष्ठं समारुह्य सुतो व्यासस्य भारत ।
समे देशे विविक्ते च निःशलाक उपाविशत् ॥

meaning.en: Climbing to a mountain ridge, Bharata, Vyasa's son sat on a level, secluded spot, free of any sharp stalk.

verses.text:
धारयामास चात्मानं यथाशास्त्रं महामुनिः ।
पादात्प्रभृति गात्रेषु क्रमेण क्रमयोगवित् ॥

meaning.en: The great sage, who knew the sequence of yogic practice, collected himself according to the rule, in order from the feet through the limbs.

verses.text:
ततः स प्राङ्मुखो विद्वानादित्ये नचिरोदिते ।
पाणिपादं समाधाय विनीतवदुपाविशत् ॥

meaning.en: Then, wise, facing east just after sunrise, he sat in a disciplined posture with hands and feet composed.

verses.text:
न तत्र पक्षिसंघातो न शब्दो नापि दर्शनम् ।
यत्र वैयासकिर्धीमान्योक्तुं समुपचक्रमे ॥

meaning.en: There was no flock of birds, no sound, and no onlooker where the wise son of Vyasa began his yoga.

verses.text:
स ददर्श तदात्मानं सर्वसङ्गविनिःसृतम् ।
प्रजहास ततो हासं शुकः संप्रेक्ष्य भास्करम् ॥

meaning.en: He saw himself freed from all attachments, and then Shuka, gazing at the sun, laughed.

verses.text:
स पुनर्योगमास्थाय मोक्षमार्गोपलब्धये ।
महायोगीश्वरो भूत्वा सोऽत्यक्रामद्विहायसम् ॥

meaning.en: Taking to yoga again to find the path of liberation, he became a great lord of yogis and rose into the sky.

verses.text:
ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा देवर्षिं नारदं तदा ।
निवेदयामास तदा स्वं योगं परमर्षये ॥

meaning.en: Then he circled the divine sage Narada and told that great sage of his yoga.

verses.text:
दृष्टो मार्गः प्रवृत्तोऽस्मि स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु तपोधन ।
त्वत्प्रसादाद्गमिष्यामि गतिमिष्टां महाद्युते ॥

meaning.en: "The path is seen and I have set out. Peace to you, wealthy in austerity; by your grace, radiant one, I shall go to the goal I wish."

verses.text:
नारदेनाभ्यनुज्ञातस्ततो द्वैपायनात्मजः ।
अभिवाद्य पुनर्योगमास्थायाकाशमाविशत् ॥

meaning.en: Permitted by Narada, Dvaipayana's son bowed, took to yoga again, and entered the sky.

verses.text:
कैलासपृष्ठादुत्पत्य स पपात दिवं तदा ।
अन्तरिक्षचरः श्रीमान्व्यासपुत्रः सुनिश्चितः ॥

meaning.en: Leaping from Kailasa's ridge, the resolute and splendid son of Vyasa, moving through the sky, flew up to heaven.

verses.text:
तमुद्यन्तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं वैनतेयसमद्युतिम् ।
ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि मनोमारुतरंहसम् ॥

meaning.en: All beings saw that best of the twice-born rising, bright as Garuda, swift as thought and wind.

verses.text:
व्यवसायेन लोकांस्त्रीन्सर्वान्सोऽथ विचिन्तयन् ।
आस्थितो दिव्यमध्वानं पावकार्कसमप्रभः ॥

meaning.en: Reflecting by his resolve on all three worlds, he followed the divine road, shining like fire and sun.

verses.text:
तमेकमनसं यान्तमव्यग्रमकुतोभयम् ।
ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि जङ्गमानीतराणि च ॥

meaning.en: All beings, moving and unmoving, saw him going with one-pointed mind, unagitated and without fear from any quarter.

verses.text:
यथाशक्ति यथान्यायं पूजयां चक्रिरे तदा ।
पुष्पवर्षैश्च दिव्यैस्तमवचक्रुर्दिवौकसः ॥

meaning.en: Then they honored him as they could and as was proper, and the dwellers in heaven showered him with divine flowers.

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताः सर्वे गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः ।
ऋषयश्चैव संसिद्धाः परं विस्मयमागताः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing him, all the throngs of gandharvas and apsaras, and the perfected sages, were filled with great wonder.

verses.text:
अन्तरिक्षचरः कोऽयं तपसा सिद्धिमागतः ।
अधःकायोर्ध्ववक्त्रश्च नेत्रैः समभिवाह्यते ॥

meaning.en: "Who is this, moving through the sky, who has reached perfection by austerity, body below and face upward, carried along by his eyes?"

verses.text:
ततः परमधीरात्मा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः ।
भास्करं समुदीक्षन्स प्राङ्मुखो वाग्यतोऽगमत् ।
शब्देनाकाशमखिलं पूरयन्निव सर्वतः ॥

meaning.en: Then, utterly steady, renowned in the three worlds, he went on facing east, gazing at the sun, restraining speech, as if filling the whole sky with sound on every side.

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं सहसा दृष्ट्वा सर्वाप्सरोगणाः ।
संभ्रान्तमनसो राजन्नासन्परमविस्मिताः ।
पञ्चचूडाप्रभृतयो भृशमुत्फुल्ललोचनाः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing him suddenly approach, all the groups of apsaras, King, were bewildered and greatly amazed, Panchachuda and others with eyes wide open.

verses.text:
दैवतं कतमं ह्येतदुत्तमां गतिमास्थितम् ।
सुनिश्चितमिहायाति विमुक्तमिव निःस्पृहम् ॥

meaning.en: "What deity is this, who has taken the highest path? He comes here, firmly resolved, as if liberated and free of desire."

verses.text:
ततः समतिचक्राम मलयं नाम पर्वतम् ।
उर्वशी पूर्वचित्तिश्च यं नित्यमुपसेवते ।
ते स्म ब्रह्मर्षिपुत्रस्य विस्मयं ययतुः परम् ॥

meaning.en: Then he passed the mountain called Malaya, which Urvashi and Purvachitti always visit; those two were greatly amazed at the brahmin sage's son.

verses.text:
अहो बुद्धिसमाधानं वेदाभ्यासरते द्विजे ।
अचिरेणैव कालेन नभश्चरति चन्द्रवत् ।
पितृशुश्रूषया सिद्धिं संप्राप्तोऽयमनुत्तमाम् ॥

meaning.en: "Oh, the concentration of this brahmin devoted to Vedic study! In no long time he moves through the sky like the moon. By serving his father he has attained an unsurpassed perfection.

verses.text:
पितृभक्तो दृढतपाः पितुः सुदयितः सुतः ।
अनन्यमनसा तेन कथं पित्रा विवर्जितः ॥

meaning.en: A son devoted to his father, firm in austerity, dear to his father: how is he separated from that father, with a mind fixed on one thing alone?"

verses.text:
उर्वश्या वचनं श्रुत्वा शुकः परमधर्मवित् ।
उदैक्षत दिशः सर्वा वचने गतमानसः ॥

meaning.en: Hearing Urvashi's words, Shuka, who knew the highest dharma, looked at all the directions, his mind on her words.

verses.text:
सोऽन्तरिक्षं महीं चैव सशैलवनकाननाम् ।
आलोकयामास तदा सरांसि सरितस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: He looked at the sky and the earth with its mountains, woods, and forests, and at lakes and rivers.

verses.text:
ततो द्वैपायनसुतं बहुमानपुरःसरम् ।
कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वा निरीक्षन्ते स्म देवताः ॥

meaning.en: Then all the divinities looked at Dvaipayana's son, with great respect, hands folded.

verses.text:
अब्रवीत्तास्तदा वाक्यं शुकः परमधर्मवित् ।
पिता यद्यनुगच्छेन्मां क्रोशमानः शुकेति वै ॥

meaning.en: Then Shuka, who knew the highest dharma, said to them: "If my father follows me, crying out 'Shuka!',

verses.text:
ततः प्रतिवचो देयं सर्वैरेव समाहितैः ।
एतन्मे स्नेहतः सर्वे वचनं कर्तुमर्हथ ॥

meaning.en: then all of you must answer him in unison; for love of me you should all do this."

verses.text:
शुकस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा दिशः सवनकाननाः ।
समुद्राः सरितः शैलाः प्रत्यूचुस्तं समन्ततः ॥

meaning.en: Hearing Shuka's words, the directions with their woods and forests, the oceans, rivers, and mountains replied to him from every side.

verses.text:
यथाज्ञापयसे विप्र बाढमेवं भविष्यति ।
ऋषेर्व्याहरतो वाक्यं प्रतिवक्ष्यामहे वयम् ॥

meaning.en: "As you command, brahmin, so it shall be indeed; when the sage speaks, we will answer."
